predecessors.name: Empire of Brazil
predecessors.text: Cisplatina, the land in Brazil's 1827 shape and not in its 1828 shape

predecessors.name: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
predecessors.text: the Eastern Province, which the Florida assembly of 25 August 1825 had declared united with the United Provinces

ledger.x: 27 August 1828: Cisplatina becomes the Eastern Republic of Uruguay.
27 August 1828: the whole of Cisplatina passes from Brazil to the new republic (the Brazil dossier records the matching loss).
February 1843: Oribe besieges Montevideo and splits the country.
1851: Oribe is defeated and the Colorados hold the whole country.
20 February 1865: the Villa de la Union accord ends the Uruguayan War.

wars.name: Cisplatine War
wars.outcome: The Preliminary Peace Convention of 27 August 1828, mediated by Britain, made Cisplatina independent as the Eastern Republic of Uruguay.

wars.name: Uruguayan Civil War (Guerra Grande)
wars.outcome: The Cerrito government of Oribe, with Rosas's forces, held the interior and besieged Montevideo from February 1843; Oribe was defeated in 1851 after Urquiza's uprising against Rosas and Brazil's May 1851 intervention, and five treaties with Brazil followed.

wars.name: Uruguayan War
wars.outcome: Brazil and the Colorados won: Flores took the presidency on 20 February 1865 under the Villa de la Union accord; Uruguay's borders did not change.

certainty.note: No treaty fixed the Brazilian frontier before 1851; the claim north of the Rio Cuareim was open.
The Brazil-Uruguay boundary is defined 'according to the 1851 border treaty'; the Isla Brasilera and Invernada (Masoller) disputes are small exceptions.
